svg.title: Native fluorescent-spot triangulation geometry — OpticalSetup setup
svg.desc: A 488 nm laser excites a small fluorescent sample. A perpendicular 50 mm lens images the emission spot onto a camera; moving the sample along the laser axis shifts its camera position. This native example uses fluorescence as the observable isotropic spot rather than unmodeled elastic surface scattering. The 2D imaging geometry is useful for triangulation, but there is no calibrated pixel-to-height conversion, 3D baseline model or surface-dependent speckle.
